To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

AIDA is a good algorithm for data access from broadcast disk environments, and pinwheel scheduling provides a good solution for data access from disk environments where the data is frequently changed at a server and needs to be available to clients upon request, where the server-to-client communication bandwidth exceeds the communication bandwidth from any single client to the server, where timely access to data is essential, and where transmission errors are possible.

(1) the AIDA/pinwheel combination can provide timely and fault-tolerated data access, and (2) the combination of AIDA and pinwheel scheduling provides a solution to the data access problem in environments where the data is frequently and unpredictably updated at a server and needs to be available to clients upon request, and the bandwidth from the server to the clients is significantly greater than the bandwidth from any single client to the server.

the combination of AIDA and pinwheel scheduling (i) provides timely data access to clients, even when the data is updated frequently at the server, (ii) provides fault-tolerant retrieval, even in the face of transmission errors, and (iii ) provides efficient utilization of the server-to-client channel bandwidth.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a class of applications where data needs to be made widely available to clients, and where timely access to the data is critical, even in the face of transmission errors.
designing a fault-tolerant broadcast data access strategy that can provide timely access to the data even under the presence of transmission and/or other errors.
the design of data access strategies for broadcast disk systems.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a novel data dissemination strategy for the broadcast disks model that is both fault tolerant and timely.

the combination of the pinwheel scheduling algorithm with AIDA is a good solution for data access in environments where the data is frequently and dynamically updated at a server and the server-to-client communication bandwidth exceeds the client-to-server communication bandwidth.
we propose a pinwheel-based scheduling algorithm that is able to provide timely and fault tolerant access to data from broadcast disks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
pinwheel-based scheduling can be used to implement a fault-tolerant, timely and efficient broadcast disk.
pinwheel scheduling can be used to design fault-tolerant, timely, and bandwidth-efficient access schemes.
pinwheel scheduling can be used to schedule AIDA-based data dissemination to ensure timely data access in the presence of errors.
